class.name: LocalPlayer
class.brief_description: One human sitting at this machine.
class.description: Owned by the [GameInstance] rather than by the game mode, so it survives a level change: the [PlayerController] dies with the old level, this does not. It holds that human's own [PlayerInput] and, for split screen, their viewport. Create them with [method World.create_local_player] or let press-to-join do it (see [member GameModeBase.allow_press_to_join]). The [GameModeBase] then logs each one in and gives it a controller.

method.name: adopt_camera
method.description: Moves a camera into this player's [member viewport_override] and makes it current there. Needed for split screen because [Camera3D] has no custom viewport - [method Camera3D.make_current] acts on the camera's nearest ancestor [Viewport], so the camera has to physically live inside the [SubViewport]. Reparenting detaches the camera from the pawn, so drive it with a [RemoteTransform3D] on the pawn afterwards. A [Camera2D] does not need this: [PlayerController] points its [member Camera2D.custom_viewport] at the right viewport by itself.

method.name: get_player_input
method.description: This player's own action state. Never null.

members.member: See [member PlayerInput.device_slots]. To go local co-op, narrow player 0 off [constant PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_ALL] first, or it will swallow every other device's input.
Position in the [GameInstance]'s list. Kept dense when a player leaves.

The [SubViewport] this player renders into, or [code]null[/code] for the shared main viewport, which is the default. The framework does not build the split screen layout - you do - it only records which viewport belongs to whom. Cleared on a level change, because the old level's viewport dies with it.
